en.name: Matthew
en.summary: A tax collector called directly from his post, traditionally credited with the first Gospel.
en.body: Matthew, also called Levi, was a tax collector in Capernaum — a profession that made him a social outcast among his fellow Jews — when Jesus called him with the simple words "Follow me." He is traditionally identified as the author of the Gospel of Matthew, which opens with the genealogy and infancy narrative of Jesus, including the visit of the Magi. Accounts of his later life and martyrdom vary widely across traditions, with some placing his death in Ethiopia.
